result.summary: Clear key and value DataStream buffers in BerkeleyROCursor::Next() before copying the next record into them. This aligns the Berkeley DB read-only cursor with SQLiteCursor and documents the replacement contract on DatabaseCursor::Next().
result.problem: During legacy wallet migration (migratewallet), record deserializers can leave optional suffix bytes unread, such as extra flag bytes in v2 key metadata. Because LoadRecords reuses the same stream instances across records and BerkeleyROCursor::Next() appends to them without clearing, leftover bytes pollute the deserialization of subsequent records and cause migration to fail with corruption errors.
evidence: The PR description notes that migratewallet rejects valid legacy wallets as corrupt when v2 key metadata includes trailing unread flag bytes, and the included regression test fails without the fix.
result.changed_since_previous: Diff provided; the implementation matches the previous description.
result.card: Clears key and value stream buffers in BerkeleyROCursor::Next() before copying each record, matching SQLiteCursor. Currently, LoadRecords reuses stream objects across records, causing unread suffix bytes from one record to contaminate subsequent records and fail legacy wallet migrations with false corruption errors. The author demonstrates this bug on old wallets with unread v2 metadata bytes, and regression coverage confirms the cursor now properly replaces stream contents. The PR has no dependencies.

risk.why: A flaw in cursor record reading during migration could misparse wallet records and cause wallet migration to fail or produce incomplete descriptor wallets.
